title: Court of Two Voices
summary: Two advocates argue opposite sides of one question, and witnesses give the same evidence to both. Arguments go to the Judge; rebuttals go between the advocates. The Judge weighs both sides and rules with reasons, and the Clerk records the ruling for later cases.
whenToUse: Decisions with real trade-offs, or where one model tends to agree with itself: choosing between designs, checking a claim, reviewing a risky change.
strengths: Both sides of a question get a strong voice
Shared evidence keeps the debate grounded
Rulings with reasons build a reusable record
risks: At least three model calls per question
An advocate may argue well for a weak position
The Judge can split the difference instead of ruling

smileMetrics.cooperation: Evidence used by both advocates, and points conceded honestly.
smileMetrics.harmony: Rulings later upheld by results ÷ rulings made.
smileMetrics.gathering: Rounds needed before the Judge can rule.

communication: Witnesses give evidence to both advocates. The advocate for speaks to the Judge, then the advocate against; rebuttals pass between the advocates. After the last round the Judge rules and the Clerk records.
cooperation: +1 per evidence item used by both sides, +2 per honest concession. Cooperation = points per round.
